editorial:
We will require three stacks in this question too, one for evaluation, another for postfix, and the last one for infix expression.

Logic:

In this question, we will traverse from the back of the expression and we will push the operands into the stack and whenever we come across an operand we will pop out two operands such that the top most one will be value1 and the next removed operand will be value2.

Infix - (value1 operator value2)

Postfix - value1 value2 operator

Let us solve this expression: -+2/*6483

We got * operator so we will pop. Remember value1= 6 and value2= 4

Evaluation=6*4= 24, infix= (6*4), postfix= 64*

We got / operator so we will pop.

Evaluation= 24/8= 3, infix= ((6*4)/8), postfix= 64*8/

+ Operator is there so we will pop again

Evaluation = 2+3=5, infix= (2+ ((6*4)/8)), postfix= 264*8/+

We got - operator so we will pop again

Evaluation= 5-3=2, infix= ((2+ ((6*4)/8))-3), postfix=264*8/+3-

At last, we got our answers in respective stacks.

Evaluation= 2

Infix expression= ((2+ ((6*4)/8))-3)

Postfix expression= 264*8/+3-
